utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: As far as you know, what was the position of Srdic in SDS around this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I really don't know. I know that earlier he was president of the SDS. What position he held in the party later on, I really don't know. He was probably a member of the leadership. What position he held exactly, I don't know. May I make an observation regarding this document? It is interesting to note that on the top it says "Serbian municipality of Prijedor; whereas, the stamp of the legal municipality is used with the words "Municipal Assembly of Prijedor," which means an attempt to legalise this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: So you are saying that the stamp, according to the text, belongs to the Municipal Assembly in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: And on 4th of May, 1992, who was functioning as president of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: In May, 1992, you are asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Yes, after the Serbian takeover.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: In May 1992 after the takeover of power, as far as I know, in my opinion, there was no legal president of the Municipal Assembly, but the illegally appointed president was Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: You mentioned that you at the meeting with president Kovacevic, the Executive Board and others in late July, early August, had expressed a wish to leave Prijedor as soon as possible. When did you actually manage to leave Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I managed to leave Prijedor in December of that year, at the end of the year, therefore.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Could you give additional information about the way you leave -- left, additional to what you mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I said earlier on that my wife tried to find a connection in Banja Luka and she managed to do that. An organisation that was engaged in the resettlement of the population asked for a certain sum, and she paid this sum, and they said they would let us know when to come. And I managed to find a former colleague from work, who used to work with me, who was a Serb, of course, because no one else could take me to Banja Luka. I had to have someone of confidence with me. And he drove us by car to Banja Luka. But there were cases that people paid to other people and after that, they lost their lives. But this man justified our trust in him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Did your whole family leave together, that is, you, your wife and your children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, we left together. In a convoy from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Did you then leave Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. I went abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Before you left Prijedor, did you have to sign any documents relevant to your property or any other documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: As I said, I personally didn't go out, but my wife had to. There were certain documents to be compiled. She had to go to the bank to get a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. certificate which would prove that she had no outstanding debts, to close some payments and some additional formalities to be completed. But we did not sign anything concerning our property.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: What were you able to bring with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Just the property that could fit in a bag, the basic necessities. The clothes to change, a little food.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: What is the status of the apartment your family used to live in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: You mean the current status?

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I really don't know. But I heard that somebody moved in shortly after that. I don't know who it was, but I think it must have been one of the deserving Serb combatants who was eventually given this apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: The Prosecution would, before we conclude, like to show the witness and introduce a few more documents. First document 111, 111 on the Prosecution 65 ter list of exhibits. The one page original has ERN number 00633929, the English translation has ERN number at the top of the page 01087486.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D

utterances.text: Do you know the ethnic religious identity of the two persons referred to in paragraphs one and two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Jakupovic, who is relieved of his duty, is a Bosniak and Jovan Vukoja is a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: As far as you know, was President Kovacevic a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I really don't know who the members of the Crisis Staff were. I never heard their names being listed, but it was my assumption that the self-appointed president of the Municipal Assembly would be one of them, the president of the Executive Board and the head of the police. But these were just my assumptions. I never saw a document to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: As far as you know, would the president of the Executive Board be a member of the War Presidency, municipal War Presidency that were to be established in times of emergency under the regime prior to the takeover?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. I think that the president of the Executive Board should be a member of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Would the president of the Municipal Assembly also be a member of the municipal War Presidency, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, I think that he would have been the president of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: The person referred to in paragraph 1, Jakupovic, was this person politically active?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: As far as I know, he used to be a member of the Assembly. He was a deputy of the socialist -- Social Democratic Party, that he was a representative of that political party. Unfortunately I heard that he was killed in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: The Prosecution would then like to show the witness and introduce document 112, 112 in the Prosecution's Rule 65 ter list of exhibits. utterances.speaker: WITNESS D

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What would be the remaining time for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution was planning to introduce three more documents and then ask four general questions, four or five general questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then, please proceed with the documents and then we have a break later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: The Prosecution would like to show the witness and introduce document 120, that is, 120. The one-page original has at the top the page ERN number 00633939. The English translation has at the top of the page ERN number 01087493.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This would then be provisionally S26.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Would the witness please read the document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: "Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Serbian municipality of Prijedor, Executive Board, number 02-111-59/92, date: 5th of May, 1992. "Pursuant to Article 78 of the Rules of Procedure of the Executive Board of the Serbian municipality of Prijedor, at its session held on the 5th of May, 1992, the government of the Serbian municipality of Prijedor adopted the following decision: "1. Iso Bucan is hereby relieved of his duty of the commander for logistics security effective as of the 5th of May, 1992. "2. This decision shall take effect on the day of its adoption and Major Radmilo Zeljaja shall see to its implementation. "President of the Executive Board, Dr. Milan Kovacevic."

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: What is the ethnic-religious identity of the persons referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The person who is relieved of his duty is a Bosniak and the person mentioned in paragraph 2 who is entrusted with the implementation of the decision is a Serb and a member of the military. This is actually the first time that I see a member of the military being involved in the decision of -- in the decision of the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Does this decision exemplify the exercise of authority of a civilian body over the military after the Serbian takeover?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I think that there is no foundation for asking this kind of question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Although the witness has apparently, to a certain extent, already answered this question, the connection seems to be clear and therefore the objection is dismissed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Does this decision exemplify the exercise of authority of a civilian body over the military after the Serbian takeover?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: In my opinion, looking at this document, I think that it is at least telling that there was close coordination between the Executive Board and the army and military authorities, that is. As I said, it is, to say the least, quite telling.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would like to show the witness and introduce document 126, that is 126, from the Rule 65 ter list of exhibits of the Prosecution. The original of this document has ERN number 00633942. The English translation has ERN number, also at the top of the page, 01087496.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Provisionally S27.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: May I ask the witness to please read the document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: "Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbian municipality of Prijedor, Executive Board, number 02-111-62/92, date: 5th of May, 1992. "Pursuant to Article 78 of the Rules of Procedure of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Executive Board of the Serbian Municipality of Prijedor, at its session held on the 5th of May, 1992, the government of the Serbian municipality of Prijedor adopted the following decision: "1. Vahid Ceric is hereby relieved of his duty of assistant commander for the organisation of mobilisation and personnel affairs, effective as of the 5th of May, 1992. "2. This decision shall take effect on the day of its adoption, and Major Radmilo Zeljaja shall be possible for its implementation. "President of the Executive Board, Dr. Milan Kovacevic."

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: And finally, Your Honours, the Prosecution would like to show the witness and introduce document 122, that is 122, from the Rule 65 ter list of exhibits of the Prosecution. The original has two pages and the first page has ERN number at the top of the page, 00634039, second page, 40, instead of 39. The English translation has in the middle of the page, ERN number 00913684, and the second page, 85, instead of 84.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This would then be provisionally S28.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: May I ask the witness to start reading this document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: "Minutes of the 2nd session of the National Defence Council of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, held on the 5th of May, 1992, starting at 1500 hours. "The session was chaired by Dr. Milomir Stakic, President of the council. "The following attended the session: Dr. Milomir Stakic, Rade Javoric, Slavko Budimir, Slobodan Kuruzovic, Dr. Milan Kovacevic, Vladimir Arsic, Simo Drljaca, Bosko Mandic and Radmilo Zeljaja, members of the council. The session was also attended by Simo Miskovic, Radenko Banovic, Ranko Travar, Vojo Pavicic, Mile Mutic and Milenko Rajlic. "The minutes were taken by Spiro Marmat. "For the purposes of this session, the following agenda was established: "1. Discussion of the decision on mobilisation and the passing of resolutions - conclusions. "Participants in the discussion included Dr. Milomir Stakic, Slavko Budimir, Radmilo Zeljaja, Vladimir Arsic and Slobodan Kuruzovic. "The discussion resulted in the following conclusions: "1. The Municipal Secretariat for National Defence is to reinforce the TO detachment and the War Unit 4777, in conjunction with the military department and in accordance with the requests made by the commanders of these units. "2. The mobilisation orders following from the decision of the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina Assembly are to be carried out, when the actual situation in the municipality renders it necessary and in accordance with the needs and a special plan, through call-up papers issued by the Secretariat of National Defence. "3. By the 8th of May, 1992, a meeting is to be organised and convened with the directors of all companies in order to brief them about the newly arisen situation and their immediate obligations. "4. It is hereby suggested to the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly to consider moving to wartime organisation and operation for some enterprises, some companies, and to adopt in relation to that appropriate decisions -- decision. "5. The competent organs of the Municipal Administration, as part of the implementation of the provisions laid down by the aforementioned decision, will have the duty to secure priority communications; secure priority supplies of food, oil products, energy and other commodities; provide a continuous monitoring of production processes and the service sector in the new circumstances, and to submit regular reports thereof to the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly. "6. A curfew is hereby introduced in the entire area of the municipality between 2200 hours and 0500 hours for all persons except those who have proper authorisations issued by the police, the military police or the Serbian Territorial Defence. "7. All paramilitary units and individuals who possess weapons and ammunition illegally are called upon to surrender them immediately, and not later than the 11th of May, 1992 by 1500 hours, to the Public Security Station in Prijedor or its nearest department. After this period, the relevant organs will start searches and seizures of any such weapons and ammunition and will apply the most rigorous sanctions. "The chairman adjourned the session at 1630. "Minutes kept by Spiro Marmat. "President of the National Defence Council, Dr. Milomir Stakic."

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: At the top of the document it is indicated that Dr. Milomir Stakic was president of the Council. How do you interpret that part of the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please read a little bit -- speak a little bit slower.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to repeat his answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the entire answer. There was no interpretation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, under normal circumstances, the president of the National Security Council is the President of the Municipal Assembly by virtue of his office. So in this case, in this newly established and illegally established government, this president would automatically become the president of the National Security Council.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: National Defence Council, correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Do you know -- do you have information about the persons listed in the subsequent paragraph and their relations with the SDS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know all these people but the leading ones were people who were appointed to these positions on behalf of the SDS. For instance, the President of the municipality, the President of the Executive Board, the commander of the Territorial Defence, those were all people that the party appointed to those positions. I know that Kurusovic, Slobodan was appointed commander of the Territorial Defence by the SDS. Simo Drljaca was also appointed by the SDS as chief of police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Who was Slavko Budimir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Slavko Budimir was one of the officers in the Department for National Defence. I assume that he was automatically appointed secretary of Secretariat for National Defence when Becir Medunjanin [phoen] was replaced. That is my assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Who was Vladimir Arsic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: He is a military man. He comes from the Garrison. He represents the army. I think he was a colonel in those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Is Simo Drljaca the chief of police you referred to earlier today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, he was appointed chief of police after the takeover of power.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Who was Bosko Mandic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Is Radmilo Zeljaja the military person referred to earlier by you this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Who is Radenko Banovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Radenko Banovic was in the secretariat for the Kadastar. He was the member of one of the secretariats in the municipality and he was a member the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: What about Ranko Travar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: And Vojo Pavicic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Vojo Pavicic earlier was deputy secretary for town planning. And he was probably now appointed head of that department.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: And Mile Mutic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Mile Mutic is one of the journalists of Radio Prijedor and Kozarski Vjesnik. Actually, as far as I know he may have been the editor in chief or even the director.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Milenko Rajlic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I am not quite sure about that. But I do know that there was a journalist by that name, if that is the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Javoric, whose name is higher up in the paragraph, who was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: He was -- he used to be in the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Are any of these persons non-Serb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: They are all of Serbian ethnic identity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, including the person who kept the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: If you go to conclusion number two, there is a reference to call-up paper issued by the municipal Secretariat for National Defence. To which extent does this paragraph suggest that the municipal administration Prijedor was supporting the general military activities in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: This is a clear conclusion that an order is being forwarded taken by the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina and there is clear indication that there is coordination between the Assembly of the Autonomous Region and the Assembly of Prijedor. So there was coordination between the two, that a military solution is being adopted that was imposed in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: And the subsequent order addressed by the National Defence Council in Prijedor is addressed to the municipal Secretariat for National Defence in Prijedor which was a part of the Municipal Administration; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: If you go to the third conclusion which refers to the ordering that a meeting take place with the directors of all enterprises, by the 8th of May 1992, in order to brief them about the new situation and their immediate obligations, does this order suggest that there was coordination between the main economic actors in Prijedor and the military activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: For me, that is exactly what it means. According to my understanding, they probably wanted to mobilisation the mechanical equipment and the other resources that the economy had in its possession for military purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have some few more questions concerning this documents. So we can break at any time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It is really well-deserved break now and we resume at 4.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated and then we continue immediately. May the witness be brought in. And we have to close at 4.45 sharp, and "sharp" means sharp, today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: We go back to the document Minutes of the Meeting of the National Defence Council on the 5th of May 1992. If we can move to conclusion seven on page two, there is a reference at the end of that paragraph to "the most rigorous sanctions." In light of your professional and other Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. experiences in Prijedor, how do you understand these words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: For me, to say the least, this conclusion sounds threatening because the application of the most rigorous sanctions, one can only imagine what that can mean. To me, that is like a death threat or threaten -- threat of arrest. It is a threatening provision in any case and it is hard to imagine what lies behind the threat, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Additional to what you have already said about this document, do you have any other observations on its significance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It is hard for me to say anything new. This is just one in a series of events, probably planned, in the process of forming an ethnically pure Serbian Krajina. The mobilisation of all forces including the economy and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Have you, in your analysis of events in Prijedor, after the Serbian takeover of power in April 1992, in your mind distinguished clearly between the National Defence Council of the Municipal Assembly and the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Most frequently and mostly actually I listened over radio Prijedor about the Crisis Staff. I didn't hear the Council of National Defence being mentioned. I didn't know it existed as such. Because my impression was the Crisis Staff was behind it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Based on the members of the council present at the meeting on the 5th of May, would there be much difference between the membership of this institution and the membership of a regular War Presidency in a municipality in a time of emergency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: In times of this danger of war, the War Presidency or the Council of Defence would not look like this in normal circumstances. Because here it is compiled quite differently. One cannot see who has which function. Because I have said already that Council for National Defence consists of the president of the municipality, the President of the executive council, the commander of the Territorial Defence, the chief for National Defence, a representative of the Garrison, the chief of police, those would be the people under legal conditions in -- under illegal conditions as we see here. I really don't know how these people were selected. They were probably all the people who were appointed to these positions that I have just listed, and some additional ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: You say, "the War Presidency or the Council of Defence." In your mind, prior to the takeover, was there a difference between a War Presidency which would be established if there was a situation of emergency or threat of war or imminent threat of war and the National Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: According to what I know, in the case of an immediate threat of war being proclaimed, as far as I am familiar with the law, because after all, this is a legal question. After the proclamation of a threat of war, the Council for National Defence is transformed into a War Presidency and the Assembly is transformed into a wartime assembly. It is called a wartime assembly. It is still operating, but it is a wartime assembly. That’s as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: So it is correct in your mind there is not a sharp distinction between a War Presidency and the Council for National Defence insofar as the War Presidency would be a transformation of the National Defence Council of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know about these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Before I close with asking some general questions, Your Honours, the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Before you leave this document, for clarification, may I put one question to the witness, please. On the last page after the name of Stakic, Dr. Milomir, we find two -- I don't know what it is. I don't want to give -- "SR" what does it mean, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: In our country, we frequently use the abbreviation "SR" following the signature. It means with his own hand. Signed himself, that that man himself signed it with his own hand. His personal signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for your clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I move on to some general questions, the Prosecution would request that the Court accept all documents introduced today into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Are we to do it document by document or our way, where package observations by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would like first to raise the issue that if we look at the document 23, 24, 25, on which Mr. Kovacevic, late Mr. Kovacevic should have been signed, we would see that all those signatures are different. So obviously, either these documents have been planted or forged or in any way illegally produced. So for us, it is absolutely not possible to accept this kind of game [Realtime transcript read in error "again"]. I would rather, on the other hand, I would also--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I interrupt you. Please don't speak of a game.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if you are aware, but the persons who collected some documents for this Tribunal have been arrested for terrorism in Sarajevo and have been processed by federation authorities, not by RS authorities. So we really have all fundaments to believe that something wrong have been done with the documentation that has been presented in front of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Of course it is the right for the Defence to demonstrate or even to prove that the document was false or was a falsification or whatever. Let's go through the documents document-by-document. May I ask that in the transcript at 16:14 the word "game" may be added. We have serious problems today with the transcripts, I am afraid. Then let's please proceed with the documents in the order of the 65 ter numbers. The first one was Exhibit former 9, now 17. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't see the signature on the document, Your Honour, at all. And we object to these documents, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: S17 admitted into evidence, and in the English version as small 'A' and the B/C/S version small 'B'. Then we turn to 87, which is S18.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We in no way can confirm the authenticity of this document because we don't know what the signature of this person - only says Director - should be. So basically the same grounds for the objection as with the previous one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence as 16A and B respectively. 95, which is now provisionally S19.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not signed. Same objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence as S19A and 19B. Former 101 now provisionally S20.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The seal used does not correspond to the function of the signee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence as S20A and 20B. Number 90, now S21.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this document, if you see it, the first page, the first paragraph, later on something has been added. The whole document has been composed in Latin letters and then, in the second row, you see Cyrillic letters. So obviously, afterwards, something had been added, obviously and not by the same person who composed. Because this is electronic version of a transmission of a document in the pash [phoen] and this has been added later on in Cyrillic. There is no possibility to transmit through the pash Cyrillic letters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any comments from the side of the Prosecutor to this document which is evidently a faxed transmission?

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Could we have the witness read what has been added in Cyrillic, or the text that is there in Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could it be provided for the witness, please. There are two parts in Cyrillic, if I can see it correctly, in the middle and at the right-hand side, over the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Could the witness first read the header of what seems to be a facsimile transmission at the top of the document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: You mean from the very beginning?

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: At the very, very top of the original document there is, in very small letters --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: -- what seems to be the header of a facsimile transmission.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: "16/04/92 10:16." Then I can't see the first few figures. Then: "7312, 566, SO, Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Could you then please read the time indication in the actual body of the text which is on the first line of the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Would you then please go down to the heading under the indication of the date and again read first the text which is in Latin letters and then read for us the text which is in Cyrillic letters.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: "To the governments of AR and SAO of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina," then comes Cyrillic, or rather: "To all Serbian municipalities."

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: To the right, partly above that heading, is there a stamp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: What does it say inside that stamp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The top line is very illegible, unclear. Probably it says the Socalist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Then the second line, "Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina"; third line, "Assembly of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Autonomous Region of Krajina."

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Is there a signature under that stamp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: The Prosecution would like to point out, Your Honours, that the document, as explained earlier by the witness, originates from the republic level of authority from the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Ministry for National Defence, whereas the addition in Cyrillic refers to local distribution, and the stamp also refers to a regional political organ with its seat in Banja Luka, as far as the Prosecution knows. And the header of the facsimile transmission also refers to a political institution in Banja Luka. The Prosecution would therefore submit that this in no way casts the authenticity of the document in doubt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would the witness be so kind and come back to the Cyrillic letters above the signature. Can you identify the word there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: As far as I am able to see, and it is quite logical, the word is "odnosna" [phoen], "that is" or "rather."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any observations from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In addition to what has been said before, does this mean that the Prosecution admits that this document has been altered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It is for the evaluation of evidence later on, and as it is said and laid down in our guidelines, the admission into evidence doesn't have any impact at all on the content of the document and it's open for any challenge of the authenticity, of course. Therefore, document S21 and 28 -- 21A and 21B is admitted into evidence. May we now turn to the former 115, now 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document I would like to comment, in conjunction with, in connection with document number 24, so we have to decide which signature is the signature of Mr. -- of Dr. -- late Dr. Milan Kovacevic, because obviously we can see that those signatures are not the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Under our guidelines, this is no reason for not admitting, so therefore this document is admitted into evidence as S22A and B. Then, it is 114, now 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The evidence S23A and B. The comparison you wanted to draw was between which documents, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 22, 23, 24. Different signatures. You can check 23 and 24, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is the Office of the Prosecutor prepared to provide expert statement on the signatures?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We are not prepared to. They have not been submitted for analysis. I would submit, from my looking at them, they appear to be the identical signature, as identical as the normal variations between one individual's signature. Obviously, if the Court instructs us, if the Court is very interested in that information, this would be -- we would have to arrange for an outside agency to conduct that analysis and we would have to obtain some originals from that person. We probably have some since he was once in custody of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We want to come back to this issue later after the Judges have conferred to this issue. May we now turn to the former 112, now as 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the third type of signature, Your Honour, from the same person. Completely different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have different documents. I can't see a signature on this document. And it is ending with 932; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 932, I can't see a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is few lines underneath, but has nothing to do with the signature from the document number 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You mean the lines within the stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. We have to come back to this as well. Admitted in to evidence as S25A and 25B. Then we have to turn to 120, now 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Also as regards to signature; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted in to evidence as S26A and S26B. The former 126, now 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Same objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted in to evidence as S27A and S27B. And finally 122, now 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Although it says, as this witness explained, that it has been signed by Dr. Stakic, there is no signature at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Judges are aware of this. Nevertheless, admitted into evidence as S28A and S28B. And once again for the clarification, also the accused should understand our proceedings, this does not mean automatically that the Judges believe this document is edited by you, Dr. Stakic. I think this was all as regards documents. Thank you. You want to proceed the last 11 minutes with the hearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Yes, we have a few more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But, please, take into account the time limit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Sir, did you yourself, when you were in Prijedor, see clear signs of coordination after the takeover of power between the Crisis Staff, the police, the military and the paramilitary groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: As far as I could conclude, or hear, I think that the most important information and the most important announcements made on the radio were done by the Crisis Staff. It was only after that, after, for example, an announcement was made that an inspection or a search for weapons would be carried out, that the police actually carried it out. That is why I believe that there was such coordination between the Crisis Staff and the relevant authorities such as the police or perhaps the military. As for the paramilitary groups, I heard that there were various such groups, but I don't know about their activity. I heard about the existence of the White Eagle, groups from Banja or Croatia, whether they had any control, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Did you hear of instances where the police or the military acted contrary to the orders and announcements originating from the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: What one could hear over the radio is what was actually carried out. That is why I am sure that there must have been some kind of coordination between all these bodies and the Crisis Staff. I don't know of any activities that would have been outside their control. I really don't know. It is possible that there were such activities, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Are you aware if the accused Stakic ever distanced himself or objected to the policies and actions of the SDS and Crisis Staff in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Given his position, as before the takeover, vice-president of the Municipal Assembly in Prijedor and his position in the SDS, do you think it would have made a difference if the accused Stakic had distanced himself or objected to the policies and actions of the SDS and the Crisis Staff in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I think that it is quite clear that had any of the leaders tried to distance himself, this would have had some effect, especially in his case who exerted considerable influence within the SDS. However, I never heard of any such cases, of any leading figures to have distanced themselves from this policy.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: What in your view given your position and experiences in Prijedor, was the purpose behind the arrests, the detention camps, the forcible transfers, the killings which happened in Prijedor after the takeover of power?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It was clear to me that they were trying to instill fear amongst the non-Serb population as a whole. Their message was that there was no place for the non-Serb population there. It was a systematic cleansing of the municipality of its non-Serb population which was carried out through the destruction of homes, the eviction from homes, the destruction of religious institutions, both Bosniak and Catholic ones. So the only conclusion is that their aim was to establish an ethnically cleansed municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: Your Honours, that was the last question the Prosecution has for the witness in the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I have the impression for the Office of the Prosecutor time is of essence as regards for 73(C).

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That is correct

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could we immediately come to this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Just to make it clear to the Court because the rules require a filing by 4.00. A motion was filed, but it could be withdrawn I believe this afternoon. Our issue is simply under Rule 73 for a matter of evidence and procedure, the only interlocutory appeals -- interlocutory appeals are allowed under two circumstances, and the first would be with leave of this Court. We are asking this Court for leave because we believe that this is a matter of general interest to proceedings before the Tribunal. The issue that we are raising is the Court's order on the identification parade or identification procedures for the witness. We think it is important that there be a standard across all Trial Chambers so that there is an appearance that there is uniform procedure used throughout the Trial Chambers in this Tribunal. So we are asking this Trial Chamber to certify this is a matter that would be of interest to all trials pending before this Court so we can get one uniform decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Observations by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Our only observation, Your Honour, is that we agreed and concurred with your opinion last week in connection with the identification process. And the part that we agree with our learned friend from the Office of the Prosecutor is that it is an important issue. But other than that, we certainly don't have a comment as to the interpretation or the difference of opinions in the various Chambers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Chamber has discussed the already yesterday announced request for a certification, and we came to the conclusion that this request has to be dismissed because no doubt its intention of all Trial Chambers in this Tribunal to come as close as possible to truth and to exhaust all possible means to come in doing so, as close as possible to truth. It is only to grant an additional mean of recognition of a person. It is not any kind of prejudice for one party because without any doubt, the two possibilities are additionally available for the parties to present photographs, and this identification in the courtroom which grants the Judges the direct impression of the testimony of a witness when seen five persons which may be taken from this Tribunal may be taken from the street of wherever as it is custom in all courtrooms in this world. And, therefore, we don't think it is necessary to have a decision on this issue, especially when the Judges of this Tribunal decided last week that in principle there should be no longer any kind of interlocutory appeal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for considering our request and giving us a ruling today. Just one other matter I have been asked to clarify. Was S24 admitted or is the Court withholding its decision on that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 24. Please help me. What is the document? One from today?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, from today. We also, by the way, just to remind the Court, we still have S12 pending we can deal with tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: A lot are pending, also some motions from your side we are expecting due to 1st of May, but 24 was admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then we have 25 seconds to go and we thereby adjourn and resume tomorrow 9.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 4.45, p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 3rd, day of April, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
